summary: Keep the autumn goat/sheep quotation attached to 94/158; give the different cattle/spring clause its own added example at 94/182.
rationale: 94/182 is related evidence, but not the source of this quoted wording or season.

summary: The goat/sheep breeding month is September, not June.
rationale: Supplied 94/158 has ilən and explicitly yaʕni bu payəz; its edition translation says September, Herbst.

summary: Correct the month from June to September
rationale: At 94/158 the Turoyo has 'bu yarḥo d ilən ... yaʕni bu payəz' (explicitly autumn), and the edition translates 'im September, d. h. also im Herbst'. 'Juni' contradicts both the month and its season. The secondary 94/182 citation is a separate attestation of the verb about cattle in spring.

summary: New box Preterit: example for sense 2 in Preterit (57/178)

data.turoyo: Fahəm, mʕašarle i kačkayo kmo waxt, fahəm ʕal i ləġaṯṯe.
data.translation: Er verstand, was sie sagten; er war ja eine Zeitlang mit jenem Mädchen zusammen gewesen und hatte die Sprache der Tauben zu verstehen gelernt.

rationale: New Preterit box and social sense 2: overt human associate and duration explain learned understanding.

summary: New sense 2: mit jemandem Umgang haben, eine Zeitlang mit jemandem zusammen sein

data.gloss: mit jemandem Umgang haben, eine Zeitlang mit jemandem zusammen sein

rationale: mʕašarle takes the human associate i kačkayo and duration kmo waxt; acquired language knowledge motivates the context, with no reproductive event asserted. One attestation; separate homonym status remains open.

data.turoyo: Məd hawi bəṯr mu ḥṣodo, kəmʕašri aʕ ʕeze ste w a ʕwone ste mat tayse, aʕ ʕeze mat tayse w a ʕwone mab barane.
data.translation: Wenn es nach der Ernte geworden ist, werden die Ziegen und die Schafe von den Böcken trächtig, (d.h.) die Ziegen von den Böcken und die Schafe von den Widdern.

rationale: Thin II Infectum sense-1 cell: female livestock subject with explicit m-marked male partners; preserves edition trächtig without requiring it as the sole gloss.

data.turoyo: Annaqla gdoṯina ʕal u šuġlo d aq qanyone. Aq qanyone bu rabəʕ komʕašri w bu saṯwo kowalle.
data.translation: Jetzt kommen wir zu der Arbeit mit den Rindern. Die Kühe werden im Frühjahr besprungen und kalben im Winter.

rationale: Thin II Infectum sense-1 cell: cattle in spring and calving in winter; quote its own text instead of the inherited pooled reference to the goat/sheep example.

after: bespringen; (intrans., weibliches Vieh als Subjekt; mit m- für den männlichen Partner) sich paaren, gedeckt werden;
rationale: The inherited female-subject example and three corpus tokens require the reproductive affected-subject use; ordinary II morphology does not justify a Detransitive label. Pregnancy itself is not asserted as the necessary lexical result.

summary: Female goats, sheep and cattle are zero-marked subjects of ordinary II kəmʕašri/komʕašri; the male partner can be m-marked. German werden ... besprungen does not supply a missing mi- Detransitive form.
The evidence does not cleanly choose mating, being covered or becoming pregnant as the exact endpoint. The clarified gloss keeps the reproductive frame without requiring pregnancy in every use.

57/178 has mʕašarle plus human associate and duration kmo waxt, explaining knowledge of a language. A separate social-company sense is warranted; intimacy, cohabitation or sexual relations are not entailed by the available verse.

Permitted lookup of both ʕšr entries confirms that ʕšr 2 means marking/indicating and does not cover social company. The new social use stays provisionally under ʕšr 1 pending etymological review, without inventing a new root entry.

The inherited citation bundles two breeding passages with different species and seasons. The proposed citation correction and separate cattle example avoid silently treating them as the same quotation.
Does II mʕašər with female livestock denote mating, being covered or becoming pregnant? Confirm m- as the male partner/source marker.
Does 57/178 mean prolonged company, cohabitation or intimate relations? Should this social use be an etymologically separate homonym rather than sense 2 under ʕšr 1?
Confirm the month ilən = September and the separation of 94/158 from 94/182 before accepting the existing-material corrections.
